raw_response:
I will not change too much from what I did before, because 7 mu is not big and I cannot afford a bad year. I have well water, so I will keep my better ground in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Last year’s way is still my base, then I adjust a little by cost and what I saw nearby. Around here, if wheat fertilizer is too light, the heads stay short. If maize is short of nitrogen after wheat, it turns pale fast. Cotton can make money, but it takes more watching and more spraying, so I will not put too much land into it. I went to middle school, and over the years I also listened to village training and fertilizer sellers, so I do look at balance, not only one bag of urea thrown everywhere. But I still do what works on fields like mine. This year I will put 5 mu into wheat-maize and 2 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use enough base fertilizer and give one topdressing, with 3 irrigations if the season stays normal. For maize after wheat, I will keep the stubble and do lighter tillage to save labor, then feed it mostly with nitrogen because maize responds quickly. For cotton, I will not save on potash or spraying, because if insects get ahead of me, I lose more money than I save. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, but I still have to leave room in the household budget for pesticide, water, and hired help at busy time.
